title: John Buck Legends
statementMd:
The problemsetters of the Gennady Needs Your Rating contest have written n𝑛 problems, but they forgot that they still have to write solutions! You know that for the i𝑖-th problem, it takes them ai𝑎𝑖 minutes to write a correct solution and bi𝑏𝑖 minutes to write an incorrect solution.

You know that the problemsetters will write exactly one solution for each problem and spend at most k𝑘 minutes in total writing solutions for all problems. For how many problems is it possible that the problemsetters write a correct solution?

More formally, count the number of values i among 1,2,…,n such that there exists some arrangement of correct and incorrect solutions for each problem, where a correct solution is written for problem i, and the total time spent writing all solutions does not exceed k. Note that the arrangements may differ for different values of i.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤t≤104). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n and k (1≤n≤2⋅105, n≤k≤109) — the number of problems and the maximum amount of time spent, respectively.

The next n lines each contain two integers ai and bi (1≤ai,bi≤104) — the times needed to write a correct solution and an incorrect solution, respectively.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105.

Additional constraint on the input: there exists some arrangement of correct and incorrect solutions such that all solutions are written in at most k minutes.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of problems that might have a correct solution.

## Note

In the first test case, problems 1, 3, and 5 might have a correct solution. For example,

- Writing correct solutions to problems 1 and 5 and incorrect solutions to everything else takes 6+5+5+1+2=19 minutes.
- Writing a correct solution to problem 3 and incorrect solutions to everything else takes 7+5+6+1+1=20 minutes.

In the second test case, it is not possible to write the correct solution since writing the correct solution takes 2 minutes and k=1.
